items.title: Validate opportunity-to-placement pipeline (DH → FA validation)
items.current_state: DH actively books work. FA publishes 200+ opportunities. No connection; FA hasn't validated whether its published opportunities actually book.
items.gap: Do FA-published opportunities actually result in bookings? Which opportunity types book fastest? What's the conversion rate?
items.why_it_matters: Without this, FA is research; with this, FA becomes a working platform. DH is the proof-of-concept contractor.
items.research_needed: DH identifies 20 FA opportunities in active markets (Michigan, Indiana, Ohio). Track: does opportunity get applications? Do any convert to bookings? What's timeline?
items.notes: DH as beta customer-zero for FA validation.

items.title: Measure work-to-CB-pipeline (DH → CB feedback)
items.current_state: DH works, CB trains. No feedback loop. CB doesn't know what skills matter most on actual gigs.
items.gap: When DH shows up on a job, what skills are most valuable? What surprises DH about real-world work vs. training?
items.why_it_matters: Feedback informs CB curriculum. CB becomes shaped by real market needs, not just theory.
items.research_needed: DH documents each gig for 30 days: skill gaps encountered, safety issues, communication challenges, what training would have helped. Monthly summary to CB team.

items.title: Validate crew scaling profitability model
items.current_state: DH operates solo. Long-term vision is crew services. No unit economics for crew model yet.
items.gap: If DH hires crew at $18/hr and contracts them out at $22/hr, is the 4/hr margin enough for overhead? What's break-even crew size?
items.why_it_matters: Without this, crew scaling is speculative. With this, go/no-go decision is data-driven.
items.research_needed: Model: contract rate - crew cost - overhead - contingency = profit margin. Test with first 2-3 crew hires; measure actual margin vs. model.

items.title: Map work experience to FA market intelligence (DH data → FA feedback loop)
items.current_state: DH books work across multiple markets (Michigan, Indiana, Ohio). FA publishes opportunities. No data sharing.
items.gap: DH's booking patterns could inform FA's market prioritization. E.g., 'Michigan has 2x more bookings than Ohio; FA should deepen Michigan research.'
items.why_it_matters: FA becomes smarter through real-world booking data. DH validates FA's market positioning.
items.research_needed: Monthly: DH shares booking summary by market (city, dates, pay, systems). FA compares to opportunity density in same market.

items.title: Validate market positioning vs. competing contractors
items.current_state: DH operates independently. No positioning analysis vs. Rhino, Guardian, Crew One, etc.
items.gap: What differentiates DH from other labor providers? Hourly rate? Availability? Skill set? Reliability?
items.why_it_matters: Without positioning clarity, crew scaling will compete purely on price. With positioning, can command premium for specialized crew.
items.research_needed: Research 5-10 competing labor providers: rate, availability, crew size, market coverage, specialization. Document DH advantages.

items.title: Measure CB graduate employment success rate
items.current_state: CB graduates are trained; DH might hire some. No tracking.
items.gap: Do CB graduates who work with DH perform better than non-CB workers? Do they stay longer? Book repeat gigs?
items.why_it_matters: Proves CB training works. Justifies CB pricing. Attracts employer investment in CB.
items.research_needed: When first CB graduate works with DH, compare performance metrics: safety record, skill demonstration, communication, repeat hire rate vs. non-CB crew.
